text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe says in an interview left and right's electoral platforms differ most over European issues and economic strategy, adds he plans to transfer part of mandatory payroll health contributions to a broader base by the summer.
-- Supermarkets group Intermarche buys controlling stake in German retailer Spar AG.
-- Junior Minister for European affairs Michel Barnier in an interview details plans for the European interior market to be debated in Amsterdam in June.
-- Saudi Arabia orders a third frigate from French navy shipyards, which is expected to guarantee some 2,600 jobs over five years.
-- France Telecom Mobiles launches new mobile telephone targeting private consumers, aiming for mass market.
LA TRIBUNE
-- OECD sees France and Germany as suffering from lack of employment reforms .
-- French businesses have had a good 1997 year so far, notably those which have international activity.
-- EU authorities criticise French state's management of insurer GAN, call for more information on state help.
L'AGEFI
-- Public works group Colas forecasts 25 billion franc turnover for 1997.

-- Draft decrees on the introduction of French private pension funds are ready to be published, may be questioned by the left-wing parties in the event of a win in the upcoming parliamentary election.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin in an interview on media and public services calls for a new law on communications, a reshuffling of the audiovisual sector, reform of aid to the media, and incentives to boost development of networks.
-- SNCF railway operator posts record 17.1 billion franc deficit for 1996, planned transfer of part of its debt to new infrastructure company is expected to help improve results for 1997.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- France Telecom aims for 10 million mobile telephone users in France in the year 2000, launches mass-market package offer.
-- Pilots at Air France strike in protest against cuts in starting salaries of new-hires.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- The CDR company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets plans to file new lawsuits against executives at Lyonnais banking units on alleged massive fraud up to 1993.
